summary:
# NOTES: *Salome's Burden; or, The Shadow on the Homes* (Eleanora H. Stooke). Single book, 18 chapters.

**Front matter:** Publisher S. W. Partridge & Co., London. Four illustrations: "Salome's fresh, sweet voice rang clearly..." (ch. 1 area), "Salome laid her head on the top rail of the gate..." (ch. 5), "She went to the front door to meet Mr. Fowler" (ch. 10), "'You'd better mind your own business, Salome Petherick.'" (ch. 15).

## Characters
- **Salome Petherick**: 14, lame from birth, uses crutches, brown hair/eyes, sunburnt. Keeps house, garden (carnations, roses, rose-bush planted by mother, chrysanthemums, fuchsia, verbena). Sweet clear singing voice; sings in church choir; favourite hymn "Abide with Me" (mother's favourite). Knits jerseys (taught by Mrs. Moyle).
- **Josiah Petherick**: father, fisherman, tall, strong, brick-red face, deep bass voice; brave at sea but "moral coward"; drinks at the "Crab and Cockle" inn. Formerly in church choir. Wife died 5 years before story.
- **Mrs. Petherick**: dead; favourite hymn "Abide with Me"; had made Salome promise to "look after poor father".
- **Mr. Amyatt**: Vicar of Yelton, elderly, iron-grey hair, stooping, thin, clean-shaven; teetotaler; ten years at Yelton; came from large manufacturing town, broken in health.
- **Mr. Henry Fowler**: tall, dark, several years older than wife, strong determined face, kind deep-set eyes; teetotaler from principle (once drank wine, regrets it); made household rule: no intoxicants in house. Swing-chair under lilac tree.
- **Mrs. Fowler**: young-looking, pretty, fair hair, blue eyes, fashionable, fretful, neurotic; secret alcoholic; first name unstated in text beyond "Mrs. Fowler"; favours Gerald.
- **Margaret Fowler**: daughter, Salome's age, bright, learning organ; devoted to father; feels unloved by mother.
- **Gerald Fowler**: ~6, fair curls, dark-blue eyes, sailor suit, spoilt, selfish, temper tantrums, later reformed.
- **Miss Conway**: governess, delicate young woman, lifelong teetotaler (father's family had drunkard); discovers mother's drinking.
- **Ross**: Mrs. Fowler's maid, well-mannered, good-tempered; mends and sews.
- **Mrs. Lute**: handsome middle-aged widow, former London neighbour; rents house at N— (whitewashed, clematis and roses); offers Mrs. Fowler and Margaret wine; later becomes teetotal.
- **Silas Moyle**: baker and village shop owner; "a man of peace"; fought Josiah. **Mrs. Moyle**: rosy, stout, kind; taught Salome knitting; took Salome in after storm and after fire.
- **Sam Putt**: pony-and-cart fish hawker.
- **Dr. Vawdry** (N—): doctor; second doctor from Plymouth.
- **Cook** (Greystone): stout, round red face, garrulous; gives Salome milk and cake; gossips.
- **Groom**: dismissed by Mr. Fowler for beer in stable.

## Places
- **Yelton**: fishing village, north coast of Cornwall. Vicarage (near church), church (grey, jackdaws in tower, organ, churchyard overlooks village and sea), Greystone (modern house on hill beyond village; lilac tree, croquet lawn), "Crab and Cockle" inn (sign: gigantic crab, minute cockle), Silas Moyle's shop, post-office two doors from inn (divided by shop).
- **N—**: nearby town, several miles; station; Fore Street; china shop; grocer's (where brandy bought).
- **Brixham, South Devon**: where Rev. Lyte wrote "Abide with Me" after sunset on shore.

## Chronology of events
**Ch I (June, summer evening):** Salome waits at gate for Josiah. Amyatt praises carnations, advises prayer and patience; she says "sometimes He seems so far away." Amyatt quotes "The eternal God is thy refuge..." Josiah returns, lightly drunk; Amyatt rebukes him ("good, sound beer"). Supper: fried eggs and bacon, hard. News: Greystone let to rich London gentleman, arriving tonight. Josiah returns to inn. Salome prays over him asleep in clothes.

**Ch II (next day):** Josiah goes mackerel fishing. Salome meets Gerald (tantrum outside gate), Miss Conway, Margaret. Gerald takes pink moss-rose and says he'll keep it. Fowlers: three-year lease, mother delicate. Salome describes crutches; Amyatt says God made her lame for a purpose. Margaret: "May I come again?" Josiah sells mackerel to Greystone cook. Evening: he takes Salome sailing, doesn't go to inn. At gate she cries "Not to-night!" He stays home. "You grow more like your dear mother."

**Ch III:** Mrs. Fowler on sofa, shattered nerves; wants wine. Margaret asks father in garden for wine for mother; he is angry, refuses, declares teetotal rule; "I bitterly regret ever having done so." Tea; Amyatt visits; Margaret to learn organ; Gerald to blow organ ("disobliging"). Gerald's sweet cakes; father refuses him more.

**Ch IV (end of July):** Mrs. Fowler meets Salome in churchyard; invites her to Greystone to sing. Salome: mother's death, her own fretfulness. Evening service: Miss Conway plays "The Heavens are telling"; Salome sings "Abide with Me." Amyatt tells Lyte's history. Salome passes inn, hears father singing drunk. Josiah at home: rails against Fowler for dismissing groom; argues about Silas's bread account; swears at Salome; she protests; he storms out.

**Ch V:** Josiah had got Silas to extend credit. Fowlers hire Josiah's boat; he rows them round rocks, earns shillings. Josiah gives Salome half-crown for Silas. Silas says Greystone's teetotalism is example. Gerald runs off to beach alone ("I can take care of myself"); Salome brings him to her garden; Miss Conway retrieves him, angry. Margaret visits Salome at garden gate; Salome sobs, reveals drinking; Margaret: "pluckiest girl I know". Invitation to Greystone next day, 5 o'clock. Margaret tells father; he: "Drink can slay affection"; "I hope you would ask God to support and comfort you."

**Ch VI (next day):** Tea under lilac tree: Mrs. Fowler, Mr. Fowler (kind to Salome; "He never sends a cross without its compensation"), Gerald, Miss Conway, Mr. Amyatt maybe. Salome sings a lullaby (mother's) and "Abide with Me." Margaret gives Salome gold shell brooch bought with own money. Mr. Fowler leaves for London next morning. Josiah waiting, sober. Josiah had argued with Fowler on beach that morning. Salome: "I'm perfectly happy... My mind's at rest!"

**Ch VII:** Mr. Fowler leaves at 7am for N— train; asks Margaret to be mother's companion. Mrs. Fowler up for breakfast. Drive to N—; meets Mrs. Lute on Fore Street; Mrs. Lute urges visit and offers Margaret wine; Mrs. Fowler accepts wine; Margaret declines. Mrs. Fowler calls teetotalism "fad". Telegram from Mr. Fowler. Midnight: Mrs. Fowler (nervous) comes to Margaret's room: "Oh, child, I wish you had a better mother." Margaret quotes "Abide with Me."

**Ch VIII:** Morning: Mrs. Fowler appears, fine; letter from husband. Afternoon drive to N— with Miss Conway and Gerald; Mrs. Fowler alone at grocer's (brandy purchase, revealed later); she is quiet on return. Evening: Miss Conway questions Margaret about Mrs. Lute's wine; she turns white. Margaret's nightmare; checks mother asleep. Next day: letter posted at post-office; Josiah staggers out of inn drunk; Silas (named "Samuel Moyle" once in text) says "poor motherless maid". Gerald mimics drunk; Miss Conway reproves. Mrs. Fowler: "Better for her if she had no father at all." Margaret: "Drink is an awful thing."

**Ch IX (next day, noon):** Yelton deserted. Margaret visits Salome, who knits navy jersey for Josiah. Margaret asks to learn knitting. Rose-bush by gate smashed by Josiah falling over it. Salome: father "says he hates teetotalers." Mrs. Fowler locks bedroom door; Margaret, Miss Conway, Ross; Mrs. Fowler opens drunk, faints; brandy bottle and glass on dressing-table. Ross swears she never supplied it. Miss Conway asks Margaret to keep Gerald; Margaret weeps that night.

**Ch X:** Miss Conway explains: Mrs. Fowler bought brandy at grocer's in N—; drinking began with fatigue and wine; illness caused by drink; Mr. Fowler became teetotal to save her. Miss Conway sat up night with Mrs. Fowler who begged for stimulant. Mr. Fowler returns (~8pm); garden talk: "Life is very hard, sometimes"; plans to invite Mrs. Lute, will explain teetotal house. Mrs. Fowler: "Father, I'm so very glad you've come home."

**Ch XI (September):** Mr. Fowler brought Mrs. Lute home; Mrs. Lute impressed by teetotalers. Fowler describes Josiah: Josiah smashed furniture, turned Salome out in night; Salome spent night at Moyles. Mrs. Fowler (overhearing) distressed; avoids Margaret. Margaret practises organ; finds Salome asleep in church pew; Salome's dream of father singing; Salome tells her "God... the only One who can help." Harvest moon. Josiah home drunk; cut cheek, black eye (from fight with Silas). Quarrel: Josiah shakes Salome, flings her; she strikes forehead on mantelpiece, unconscious.

**Ch XII:** Amyatt, back from fishing, told by Silas. Finds Salome apparently dead; Josiah wails; Amyatt revives her. Josiah apologises; Amyatt urges pledge; Josiah refuses. Mrs. Moyle comes to stay night; warns Josiah he must "choose between drink and Salome"; "you're killing her by slow degrees." Josiah apologises to Silas. Salome poorly a week; villagers' pity. Margaret visits; Salome says father will be steadier. Fowler: Josiah "loves drink even better." Within a fortnight Josiah drinks heavily again. Silas grumbles but keeps supplying bread.

**Ch XIII (autumn):** Margaret visits Mrs. Lute at N— for a fortnight; estrangement with mother; servants blame Mrs. Fowler's favouritism. Equinoctial gales; no fishing; Pethericks short of food. Salome visits Greystone; cook gossips (mistress wanted to take Gerald to town, not Margaret). Salome tells Mrs. Fowler of debt (nearly 18 shillings). Mrs. Fowler gives a sovereign. Mrs. Fowler: "Go on loving your father." Josiah: "She's a real kind lady, anyway."

**Ch XIV (stormy night, autumn):** Schoolroom with Miss Conway, Margaret, Gerald (cat). Wind; Gerald wants a wreck; Josiah seen tarring boat. Gerald sneaks out at night. Salome sings "Lead us, heavenly Father, lead us." Margaret arrives hatless: "We've lost Gerald." Salome goes out; meets Josiah and fishermen; Josiah sends girls back. Miss Conway at cottage. Josiah carries Gerald in from boat-shelter. Gerald: "There is no wreck."

**Ch XV:** Gerald locked in bedroom for a day. Margaret falls ill (cold → inflammation of lungs), delirious, believes Gerald drowned. Ross nurses. Cook gossips. Dr. Vawdry. Salome at Vicarage gate; blames Gerald; Gerald: "mind your own business, Salome Petherick." Josiah stays home all night (had catch of fish).

**Ch XVI:** Mr. and Mrs. Fowler return ~10pm. Miss Conway tells all. Mr. Fowler stern: "indulgence." Mrs. Fowler recognises her weakness; now sees total abstinence necessary. Second doctor from Plymouth. Mrs. Fowler nurses Margaret tenderly. Crisis passes. Salome's posy (chrysanthemums, verbena, fuchsia): "Salome sent them to you with her love." Margaret prefers Miss Conway/Ross; Mrs. Fowler hurt. Margaret, in quilted silk dressing-gown from London. Gerald: "I prayed to God to make you well." Gerald says Josiah drunk nightly; Mrs. Fowler blushes.

**Ch XVII (November):** Mild month. Salome accompanies Mrs. Fowler and Margaret to N—. Mr. Fowler: Salome "badly fed, works hard." One night "Fire!": Josiah, drunk, pulled lamp off table; cottage gutted; Salome raises alarm; Silas and Mrs. Moyle; all possessions burnt; furniture uninsured. Josiah: "I'm ruined." Salome lodges with Moyles. Mrs. Fowler visits Salome, then Josiah at gate with Amyatt; urges pledge; Josiah: "I'll be a teetotaler if I can; but... won't pledge myself." Mrs. Fowler: "I will certainly take the pledge." Josiah: "I don't see that I can say 'no' to that." Mrs. Fowler tells Margaret; reconciliation: "a black shadow over my life."

**Ch XVIII (June, next summer):** Eight months after fire; Pethericks' new red-brick cottage with bow window; ivy; furniture gifts (Mrs. Moyle's dinner set; Vicarage bedding; Mrs. Fowler's chairs). Josiah pledged teetotaler, now in choir. Margaret: "that trouble... is it gone?" "Yes." Margaret: Salome taught her "what love ought to be". Gerald improved. Mrs. Lute returns, has banished intoxicants from her house. Mrs. Fowler's "Cornish roses". Final scene: Sunday evening, church, congregation sings "Abide with Me"; closing lines quoted: "Heaven's morning breaks, and earth's vain shadows flee; / In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me."

**Printer:** Whitefriars Press Ltd., London and Tonbridge.

## Key quotations
- "The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms." (Amyatt, ch. I)
- "Abide with me; fast falls the eventide..." (hymn, ch. IV)
- "Drink can slay affection." (Fowler, ch. V)
- "He never sends a cross without its compensation." (Fowler, ch. VI)
- "Drink is an awful thing." (Margaret, ch. VIII)
- "We cannot tell how much our patience and our love may be tried..." (Fowler, ch. V/IX)
- "Father, I'm so very glad you've come home." (Margaret, ch. X)
- "There is no wreck." (Gerald, ch. XIV)
